rationale: The scientific task, public contract and grader are internally consistent and well evidenced, but one control record has a wrong expected-outcome annotation, which blocks acceptance on this pass. Verified: (1) Source coverage is complete — the pyhmmer msa_to_hmm notebook has exactly two terminal products (the plan7 profile HMM via build_msa/hmm.write and the hmmsearch domain table via search_hmm/hits.write(format="domains")); both are staged, recomputed (reference hash match) and exported with verified hashes; the hmm.consensus inspection and print(ali) are correctly source-backed display exclusions. (2) Dependency hygiene is sound — the bundled prebuilt pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm fixture was compared against the reference model body and removed with a verified absence receipt (`excluded_files_absent: true`) and a re-run that still produced both endpoints; remaining LuxC-stem wheel files are byte-identical inputs or non-endpoint fixtures, and the vendor/hmmer copy does not ship in wheel installation paths. (3) The comparison contract is well defined and non-contradictory: the HMMER3 banner/DATE/COM lines are excluded (replay observations confirm these are the only run-to-run variation; domtbl is byte-stable), tolerances (2e-5 absolute for 5-decimal HMM parameters; 0.06 for 1-decimal scores/bias; 0.006 for 2-decimal acc; 5% relative E-values with a stated max-magnitude denominator) are publicly disclosed with serialization-backed rationales and boundary probes on both sides; row pruning, padding, reordering, non-finite values, malformed rows, extra outputs/ layer, missing files and cross-file query mismatches are each rejected by an executed control. Placement records confirm the grader reads LuxC.hmm/LuxC.domtbl directly under the submission root. (4) Base-question prose checks out against the actual files: the Stockholm alignment has 13 sequences and 400 columns, #=GF GA/TC/NC lines whose first pair is what the Easel parser (like hmmbuild) carries to GA -133.50/-133.50, TC -133.50/-133.50, NC -133.70/-133.70 in the reference and independent outputs; LENG 400; E≤10 thresholds are hmmsearch defaults; the reference domtbl has 12 rows in best full-sequence E-value first order with no ties; cross-file name/accession/length consistency holds and is independently checked. (5) The descriptor's tolerance claims match the executed code. The cross-engine portability limits are honestly disclosed rather than claimed, and the internal check_description_updates field is empty, so no re-annotated controls need semantic re-verification. The single defect is the expected-check annotation for the coordinates-and-description probe: it is a suite-level expected-outcome mismatch, inexpensively fixable without weakening any rule or changing any frozen mutation or scientific content, so the candidate requires revision rather than blocking.

source_coverage.rationale: The pinned source (pyhmmer msa_to_hmm notebook, adapted only to repoint two input paths) has exactly two terminal scientific products: the Plan7 profile HMM built from the Stockholm alignment via builder.build_msa, serialized by hmm.write (LuxC.hmm, 187,150 bytes in the reference), and the domain hits from pipeline.search_hmm serialized by hits.write(format="domains") (LuxC.domtbl, 4,093 bytes, 12 rows). Both were recomputed and independently obtained with matching hashes after normalization of the run-specific HMMER3 banner/DATE/COM lines, which the replay observations confirm are the only run-to-run variation. The two excluded branches are correctly diagnosed as displays, not endpoints: hmm.consensus is an interactive inspection whose information is fully contained in the HMM's CONS/MAP lines, and print(ali) shows the top domain alignment whose data (target, coordinates, scores) is fully retained in LuxC.domtbl; neither computes an independent quantity, and plan.json makes the same source-backed exclusions. GA/TC/NC carry-through matches the actual alignment annotation (first numeric pair of each #=GF line, matching Easel/hmmbuild behavior) in both the reference and independent runs. No input or method was changed relative to the source; both endpoints are requested, withheld and independently recomputed, with no supplied intermediates. No omitted scientific branches, unsupported coverage claims or scope changes were found. The single suite-level defect (a probe's expected-check list naming domtbl_structure for a within-range coordinate mutation that the structure check correctly lets pass) does not involve source coverage, and fixing it should not alter the scientific contract; controls must be re-executed after the correction.
